original_question: A strict GKK matrix is a P-matrix for which the weak sign-symmetry inequalities A[alpha, beta]A[beta, alpha] > 0 hold for all almost principal minors, meaning minors of dispersal 1. Is every strict GKK matrix positive stable, and, more specifically, is every strict GKK tau-matrix positive stable?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 1a, "Strict GKK matrices: stability"; Problem 1 immediately above it provides the setup, but the draft is specifically targeting Problem 1a. ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper quite closely: it correctly identifies a strict GKK matrix as a P-matrix with strict sign-symmetry inequalities on all almost principal (equivalently, dispersal-1) minors, and it asks exactly the two stability questions posed in Problem 1a. It also uses "positive stable," which is the paper's term before it is shortened to "stable." ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))
missing_details: The paper works with arbitrary finite complex square matrices A ∈ C^{n×n}; this ambient field and the quantifier "for every n and every such A" are implicit in your draft. ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))

To be fully stand-alone, the notation A(α,β) for submatrices and A[α,β] for minors should be specified, together with the condition that α and β have equal cardinality. ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))

Your draft does not define a τ-matrix. In the paper, this means: define l(B):=min(σ(B)∩R), with min ∅ := ∞; A is an ω-matrix if l(A(α,α)) ≤ l(A(β,β)) < ∞ whenever ∅ ≠ β ⊆ α; and A is a τ-matrix if additionally l(A) ≥ 0. ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))
"Positive stable" should be made explicit as: every eigenvalue of A lies in the open right half-plane. ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))

To mirror the paper exactly, the target is the two-part open problem in Section 3, Problem 1a, which is presented as a follow-up to Problem 1 about approximating GKK matrices by strict GKK matrices. ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))
refined_question: For every n ∈ ℕ and every complex matrix A ∈ C^{n×n}, write A[α,β]=det A(α,β) for minors of submatrices indexed by α,β ⊆ {1,…,n} with |α|=|β|, and call A[α,β] almost principal if its dispersal |α|−|α∩β| equals 1. If A is a strict GKK matrix, meaning that A is a P-matrix (all principal minors A[α,α] are positive) and A[α,β]A[β,α] > 0 for every almost principal minor, must A be positive stable (that is, must every eigenvalue of A have positive real part)? More specifically, if A is also a τ-matrix in the sense that l(B):=min(σ(B)∩R) with min ∅ := ∞, A satisfies l(A(α,α)) ≤ l(A(β,β)) < ∞ whenever ∅ ≠ β ⊆ α, and l(A) ≥ 0, must A be positive stable? ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: After the paper's convention that "stable" means "positive stable," the official formulation is: "Are strict GKK matrices stable? Are strict GKK τ-matrices stable?" ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))
justification: The nearest official statement is not a broader conjecture about GKK or τ-matrices in general, but precisely Section 3, Problem 1a. Section 2 supplies the definitions needed to make that problem self-contained: P-matrix, sign-symmetry, weak sign-symmetry, almost principal/dispersal-1 minors, strict GKK, ω-matrix, τ-matrix, and positive stability. Section 1 explains the motivation: unstable GKK τ-matrices were already known, and the note asks under what additional conditions a GKK τ-matrix is stable. The rewrite therefore stays narrow, keeps the exact two-part scope of Problem 1a, and only adds the definitions that the paper treats as nearby context. ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))
